answer: Staked bonds make sybils expensive: each new agent must lock a copper-denominated deposit that only honest, peer-attested work slowly unlocks, the way a lotus must root before it flowers. Spin up a thousand fake identities and you post a thousand bonds up front; a single proven fraud slashes the batch, bleeding loss across them like pigment soaking through paper. The attacker pays real capital per identity before earning a cent, so scale stops being free.
